Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. Good problem to have.

High level options we can offer quickly:
1) Pro-rata uplift for remainder of current term: add the incremental units starting next invoice; charge for new units pro-rated from the change date through your current renewal date (no long-term commitment). No discount on the uplift beyond standard volume pricing.

2) Co-term + annualize + one-time credit: if you commit to the new baseline for the next 12 months and move to a single annual term (co-term existing line items), we can apply a one-time credit equal to a percentage of the pro-rated uplift to reflect the committed volume. Typical band: 5–15% credit depending on the uplift size and payment terms.

3) Hybrid: immediate pro-rated activation + a path to convert to co-term within 30 days for a reduced credit (we can backdate credit to the uplift start date if contract is executed within that window).

I'll need finance to approve the exact credit band for a 75% uplift; copying Rishi and Monica to confirm internal pricing flexibility. If you want a firm quote, Ben, can you share preferred target ARR or budget for the baseline so we can size the credit?

If helpful, I can draft a short amendment showing both pro-rata and co-term scenarios (we often do a single-row amendment + priced appendix).

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aisha — thanks for the context. Here's what I recommend based on current discount rules and precedent: 

- Up to 30% uplift: autonomous approval up to 8% one-time credit (AE approval ok).
- 30–80% uplift: require RevOps review but we can approve up to 12% one-time credit; if customer annualizes and pre-pays, move to 15% credit (needs legal/finance sign-off but typically slotted).
- >80% uplift: executive approval required (commercial review).

Given Nexura is at ~75% uplift, we can offer a 12% one-time credit if they sign the co-term amendment within 10 business days and agree to the 12-month commitment. If they pre-pay Net 30 we can push to 15% but that will need a written approval from VP Sales.
